fields.instantUtc: An instant, ISO 8601 with Z, to the second. Years before 1 are astronomical and signed: -4712 is 4713 BC. The Julian calendar before 1582-10-15 and the Gregorian from it; 1582-10-05 to 1582-10-14 never happened and are invalidInput. siderealTime and horizontal read it as UT1.
fields.julianDay: Days since noon on 1 January 4713 BC in the Julian calendar, with a fraction. Every day is 86,400 s: no leap seconds.
fields.date: A calendar date, YYYY-MM-DD, with astronomical years: 1 BC is 0000 and earlier years are negative, like -4712-01-01
fields.decimalYear: The year plus the days before the date over the days in its year, as in the wmm file
fields.deltaTInSeconds: TT minus UT1: USNO's observed monthly values from 1973-02-01, then its quarterly predictions to the file's expiry. Outside that, outOfRange.
fields.localSiderealTimeInHours: Local mean sidereal time: Greenwich plus longitude over 15, in 0 to 24
fields.rightAscensionInHours: 0 to 24, a sky position's east–west angle
fields.declinationInDegrees: −90 to 90, a sky position's angle north of the celestial equator. Not the magnetic one, which is always magneticDeclinationInDegrees.
fields.azimuthInDegrees: 0 to 360, clockwise from north, from the hour angle: local mean sidereal time minus right ascension. Left out where it's undefined: at a pole.
fields.altitudeInDegrees: −90 to 90, up from the horizon. Geometric: no refraction.

cases.note: 1582-10-04 in the Julian calendar is followed by 1582-10-15 in the Gregorian.
Year 0 is 1 BC, a Julian leap year.
Noon on 1 January 4713 BC, written -4712: Julian day 0.
Julian day 0 is -4712-01-01 in the Julian calendar.
A fraction just under .5 is still the day before.
Greenwich mean sidereal time at the J2000 epoch.
At 180°, local is Greenwich plus 12 hours, wrapped.
Below the horizon: a negative altitude, not an error.
At a pole azimuth is undefined: only altitude is compared.
